warning: These prompts are original starter triage prompts, not verbatim nor complete W3C questionnaires. Consult source documents before claiming a formal review.

questions.prompt: Does the technology define interoperable accessibility semantics and names where relevant?
questions.why: Semantics must be available to user agents and assistive technology.

questions.prompt: Can users interact without relying on a single input modality?
questions.why: Keyboard, pointer, speech and other modalities should not be excluded by design.

questions.prompt: Can user preferences such as reduced motion, contrast or text presentation be respected?
questions.why: Specifications can constrain implementation support for preferences.

questions.prompt: Are alternatives available for non-text and time-based information where applicable?
questions.why: Content alternatives may require specification-level mechanisms.

questions.prompt: Are language and text direction representable when needed?
questions.why: Language and direction influence rendering and assistive technologies.

questions.prompt: Does the technology preserve Unicode and diverse scripts?
questions.why: Text processing must not assume one script or repertoire.

questions.prompt: Are locale-sensitive presentation and input needs addressed?
questions.why: Dates, numbers, names, segmentation and input vary by locale.

questions.prompt: Does the specification identify collection or exposure of personal data?
questions.why: Assess unnecessary data exposure and data minimization.

questions.prompt: Could the technology enable tracking or fingerprinting?
questions.why: Multiple apparently harmless signals can identify users.

questions.prompt: Are privacy-related controls, consent and retention implications discussed?
questions.why: Reviewers need to understand control and data lifetime.

questions.prompt: Does the specification identify attacker capabilities and trust boundaries?
questions.why: Security review needs a threat model.

questions.prompt: Does the technology address permission, origin isolation and authorization where relevant?
questions.why: APIs can expose cross-origin or privilege boundaries.

questions.prompt: Are integrity, secure transport and downgrade risks considered?
questions.why: Security properties must survive the surrounding protocol.

questions.prompt: Does the feature fit established Web platform design principles?
questions.why: Avoid incompatible or unnecessarily duplicative mechanisms.

questions.prompt: Are feature detection and graceful fallback possible?
questions.why: Interoperability and progressive enhancement reduce exclusions.

questions.prompt: Are extensibility, versioning and compatibility effects considered?
questions.why: A specification must remain implementable over time.

questions.prompt: Could the technology materially change energy demand during use?
questions.why: Consider device, network and supporting service energy. Experimental draft.

questions.prompt: Could the design increase network traffic, computation or storage demands?
questions.why: Look at lifecycle workload, not just page weight. Experimental draft.

questions.prompt: Could the design shorten device or browser support lifetimes?
questions.why: Compatibility can affect hardware replacement and e-waste. Experimental draft.

questions.prompt: Are water use and infrastructure consequences considered where material?
questions.why: Consider data-center and manufacturing implications without inventing metrics. Experimental draft.

questions.prompt: Are assumptions, trade-offs and measurable impacts documented?
questions.why: Distinguish measured effects from estimates and speculation. Experimental draft.

questions.prompt: Could wider adoption produce rebound or indirect effects?
questions.why: Efficiency gains do not guarantee lower aggregate impact. Experimental draft.
